132921.subject: Zoology
132921.text: Read the following description carefully: "When more than one adaptive radiation appeared to have occurred in an isolated geographical area (representing different habitats), it leads to the development of organisms with similar functional traits from different ancestral stocks." Identify the evolutionary phenomenon described above and select the pair of organisms that best exemplifies it.
options: Convergent evolution; Placental wolf and Tasmanian wolf
Convergent evolution; Wings of butterfly and bird
Divergent evolution; Forelimbs of whale and bat
132921.sol: According to NCERT, when more than one adaptive radiation appears to have occurred in an isolated geographical area (representing different habitats), the phenomenon is termed convergent evolution. A classic example of this is the parallel evolution of Australian marsupials and placental mammals. They underwent separate adaptive radiations but evolved similar phenotypes due to similar ecological niches (e.g., the marsupial Tasmanian wolf and the Placental wolf). Darwin finches represent a single adaptive radiation.

133247.subject: Zoology
133247.text: What happens to the size of the thymus as a person grows?
133247.sol: The primary lymphoid organs in the human body are the bone marrow and thymus, where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes. The thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age. By the time puberty is attained, it reduces to a very small size. The spleen mainly contains lymphocytes and phagocytes. It acts as a filter of the blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms. It also has a large reservoir of erythrocytes.
